ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Hemophilia is an X-linked disease associated with the inability to produce specific proteins in the blood-clotting pathway. In this Figure, the family members afflicted with the disease are shown with filled-in squares (male) or circles (females). A couple is trying to determine the likelihood of passing on the disease to their future children (represented by the ? symbol above) because the hemophilia runs in the woman's family. Assuming that the woman in the couple is a carrier, what is the probability that the couple's first son will have hemophilia?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a pedigree chart with a legend indicating squares are males and circles are females; filled-in symbols indicate family members affected with hemophilia. In the lower right, an unfilled circle and an unfilled square form the couple, with a “?” below them connected by a vertical line to indicate a future child. Hemophilia is X-linked, and the question assumes the woman in this couple is a carrier. Thus the woman can be represented as XH Xh, while the unaffected father is XH Y. Because the child considered is a son, he receives the Y chromosome from his father and one X chromosome from his mother. The carrier mother passes the hemophilia-associated X allele to a son with probability 1/2, so the probability that their first son will have hemophilia is 0.5.
